title: Slips, Trips & Falls
blurb: Why slips and trips matter, and the make-safe-then-report habit that stops them.
siteNotes: Where wet floor signs, mops and spill kits are kept in each area (your manager will show you).
Who your line manager is on each shift, and how to tell them.
legalNotes: Employers must keep staff and visitors reasonably safe, and staff must take reasonable care and co-operate: Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974, ss. 2 and 7. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1974/37

CHECK: the trainer says slips, trips and falls make up "around 30%" of workplace injuries in hospitality, are the most common cause of major injuries, lead to "hundreds of thousands" of lost working days and cost businesses "more than £500 million" a year. These are HSE-style headline figures but may be dated and are national rather than hospitality-specific; please confirm against current HSE statistics. The slides repeat them as the trainer states them.
See also the 10mt-07 session on reporting and the earlier slips, trips and falls session in the library.

cards.title: Slips, Trips & Falls
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- explain why slips, trips and falls matter
- make a hazard safe straight away
- report it to your line manager

cards.title: Simply walking around can be risky
cards.body:
Slips, trips and falls are the single most common cause of accidents in hospitality businesses, around 30% of all workplace injuries. They are also the most common cause of major injuries, such as broken bones and nasty sprains.

These accidents hurt real people: guests, colleagues and ourselves.

items.label: cause of major injuries in our industry

cards.title: Do something about it
cards.body: The most important thing is to be vigilant: keep your eyes open and DO SOMETHING about any hazard you spot. Do not assume it is someone else's job.

cards.title: Make safe, then tell
cards.body: The first step is always to make the area safe. Once you are sure it is safe, the second step is just as important: tell your line manager. We need to know a hazard was there so we can look into why, and stop it happening again.

items.title: 1. Make it safe
items.text: Wet floor sign, mop it up, or move the cable or box.

items.title: 2. Tell your line manager
items.text: So we can find out why and stop it happening again.

cards.title: What helps
cards.body: Good footwear (non-slip, closed-toe), clear walkways, good lighting and cleaning up as you go all help too.

cards.title: Behind every number is a person
cards.body: Slips, trips and falls lead to hundreds of thousands of lost working days every year and cost businesses more than £500 million. Behind every one of those numbers is someone in pain and a team left short-handed.

right.title: Do not
items: Assume it is someone else's job

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Slips, trips and falls are the most common cause of accidents in hospitality
- If you spot a hazard, do something about it
- First make the area safe, then tell your line manager
- Wear non-slip, closed-toe footwear and keep walkways clear
- Never leave it for someone else

cards.q: Slips, trips and falls account for around 30% of accidents in hospitality businesses.
cards.why: They are the single most common cause of accidents in hospitality, around 30% of all workplace injuries.

cards.q: A vacuum cleaner's trailing power cord could be a trip hazard.
cards.why: A vacuum left out with its lead trailing across a corridor is a trip hazard. Do something about it.

cards.q: Roughly how much do slips, trips and falls cost businesses each year?
cards.why: They cost businesses more than £500 million a year, as well as hundreds of thousands of lost working days.

cards.q: What is the FIRST thing you should do when you come across a slip, trip or fall hazard?
cards.why: The first step is always to make the area safe, for example with a wet floor sign, mopping up or moving the hazard.

cards.q: After making it safe, what is the SECOND thing you should do?
options: Wait to see if it happens again
Add it to the next team meeting
cards.why: Tell your line manager, so we can look into why it happened and stop it happening again.

cards.q: If you see a spill but you're busy, it's fine to leave it for someone else.
cards.why: Do not assume it is someone else's job. Do something about any hazard you spot.

cards.q: Which of these helps prevent slips and trips?
cards.why: Good footwear (non-slip, closed-toe), clear walkways, good lighting and cleaning up as you go all help.

cards.q: Slips and trips are the most common cause of MAJOR injuries in hospitality.
cards.why: They are the most common cause of major injuries, such as broken bones and nasty sprains.

cards.q: You spot a spillage. What should you grab first?
options: Your phone to take a photo
A colleague to come and look
cards.why: Put a wet floor sign over the spillage, then mop it up, so nobody walks into it.

cards.q: Which footwear feature helps prevent slips at work?
cards.why: Non-slip, closed-toe footwear helps prevent slips.
